cards.text: Paul is writing to the believers in Ephesus (Eph 1:1). He just told them to forgive each other, just as in Christ God forgave them (Eph 4:32). Now he tells them to copy somebody, as beloved children.

cards.question: Who does Paul tell the believers to imitate, as beloved children?

cards.text: Then Paul tells them to walk in love. Kids copy EVERYTHING, friend: Chip spent a whole week trying to wiggle a mustache he does not have.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers to walk in love. What does he point to as the picture of that love?

answers.text: Christ giving Himself up for us
God forgiving Israel again and again
The church sharing all it had

cards.question: Paul says Christ gave Himself up for us as a fragrant sacrificial ___ to God.

cards.text: Then Paul turns a corner. Among the saints, some things have got to go: sexual immorality, any kind of impurity, and greed.

cards.question: Paul says a little greed is okay among the saints, as long as it stays small.

cards.text: Same goes for the mouth: no obscenity, foolish talk or crude joking, because those are out of character. And I say that as a stamper who can NOT stop joking, so mine stay CLEAN.

cards.question: Instead of crude joking and foolish talk, Paul says there should be ___.

cards.text: Then Paul says there's one thing you can be sure of. And it's about the kingdom of Christ and of God.

cards.question: Paul says an immoral, impure or greedy person still has an inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.
Paul adds a little side note about the greedy person. He says the greedy person is also what?

cards.text: Then comes a warning: "Let no one deceive you with empty words." Paul says that because of such things, something is coming on the sons of disobedience.

cards.question: Because of such things, what does Paul say is coming on the sons of disobedience?
Paul tells the believers to join in with the sons of disobedience so they can win them over.

cards.text: Paul says the believers were once darkness, but now they are light in the Lord. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me: light is a BIG upgrade.

cards.question: Now that the believers are light in the Lord, how does Paul tell them to walk?

cards.text: And light grows something. Paul says "the fruit of the light consists in all goodness, righteousness, and truth."

cards.question: Paul tells the children of light to test and prove what pleases other people.

cards.text: Then Paul says to have no fellowship with the fruitless deeds of darkness. Notice that: the light has fruit, and the darkness has none.

cards.question: Children of light shouldn't join in the fruitless deeds of darkness. Instead, Paul says to ___ them.

cards.text: Paul says it's shameful even to mention what the disobedient do in secret. He doesn't name a single one of them here.
But everything exposed by the light becomes visible. Believe me, when that drawer finally opened, every dusty receipt in there was suddenly VERY visible.

cards.question: Paul says everything the light shines on becomes a light itself.

cards.text: Then Paul quotes a wake-up call: "Wake up, O sleeper, rise up from the dead". This is the one alarm you do NOT hit snooze on.

cards.question: The call tells the sleeper to wake up and rise from the dead. What does it say will happen then?

answers.text: Christ will shine on the sleeper

cards.text: So Paul says, pay careful attention to how you walk: not as unwise, but as wise. Like crossing my bakery at night with the lights off, you watch EVERY step.

cards.question: Paul says to redeem the time, because the days are ___.
So don't be foolish, Paul says, but understand what the Lord's ___ is.

cards.text: Then Paul compares two ways to get filled up. Don't get drunk on wine, he says, which leads to reckless indiscretion.

cards.question: Instead of getting drunk on wine, what does Paul tell the believers to be filled with?

cards.text: Next up: psalms, hymns and spiritual songs. Paul says to sing and make music in your hearts to the Lord, which is GREAT news for a stamper who sings like a stuck drawer.

cards.question: Paul says to keep psalms, hymns and spiritual songs to yourself, and never speak them to one another.
Paul tells the believers to give thanks to God the Father for everything, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. How often?

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 13 quotes "Let no one deceive you with empty words.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This is Paul's first appearance, but the card never says who he is. It just says "Paul is writing to the believers in Ephesus." It should introduce him simply, for example "Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus" (Eph 1:1).

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke invents a new event from Papa Dorin's past: Chip spending a week trying to wiggle a mustache. That moment would have happened in the Millers' kitchen, not his bakery, so it adds to his backstory and family story.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The setup on card 6 already says greed has "got to go" among the saints. That answers card 7 before it is asked (whether a little greed is okay), so the true or false becomes a giveaway. The setup should stop short of the ruling, or card 7 should test something card 6 doesn't state.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card ties "(that is, an idolater)" only to the greedy person. In the BSB of Ephesians 5:5, the parenthesis follows the whole list "No immoral, impure, or greedy person," so the verse leaves open whether it describes the greedy person alone or all three. Both the setup ("a little side note about the greedy person") and the question close that question.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The two wrong answers, "short" and "few," mean nearly the same thing. A baker can rule them both out because only one answer can be right, which leaves "evil" by elimination. No story card sets up verse 16 either, so the card is a word-ending guess solved by a trick of the answer set.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The joke calls making music in your hearts "GREAT news" for a stamper who can't sing. That suggests the verse lets you keep the songs inside. But Ephesians 5:19 also says to speak to one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, and card 18 tests exactly that. The joke muddies the fact and nudges the baker toward the wrong answer on card 18.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it.
